To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in shell-model (SM) calculations for N =Z nuclei, in which deformations are induced by varying single-particle energies (SPE), the total Gamow-Teller strength decreases monotonously as B(E2) from the GS to the first 2+ state increases, and that similar trends are also observed for the double GT and the spin part of total M1 strength.

the total GT + and E2 strength in shell-model calculations are strongly correlated, and that the correlation can be used to estimate the total GT + strength in nuclei that do not have measured values.
the total GT + strength and the E 2 strength are correlated in N = Z nuclei.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quenching problem of the total Gamow-Teller strength.
the correlation between the quench of GT + strength and the increase in E2 strength in N = Z nuclei.
a correlation between the quenchings of the total β + GT+ strength and of the E2 strength, which are both induced by the deformation of the nuclear wave functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quenching is correlated with the increase of the E2 strength.
the quenching in the total GT strength is related to the E2 strength.

the decrease of the total GT + strength with increasing B (E2), which is observed in many nuclei, is a consequence of a decrease of the GT + strength to the first excited 2 + state and of the double GT strength, while the strength to the higher-lying 2 + states increases with B (E2).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quenching and the increase of the E2 strength can be related to the same physical origin.

a strong E2 transition from the ground state of a nucleus to the first excited state of the same spin and parity is accompanied by a significant reduction of the total GT + strength and the double GT amplitude.
the total GT strength is correlated with the E2 strength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there exists a correlation between the total GT + strength and the E1 or E2 strengths in the N = Z nuclei.
the GT+ strength is quenched when a nucleus becomes more deformed.
the total β + GT + strength is a sensitive probe of the deformation in nuclei.
